description: Measure same-future Error-return-before-Response in the real pipeline decoder, with real built-in completion producers and an independent permitted-order control.

harness.description: TestAssurancePipelineResponseOrder runs decoder_timeout, decoder_success, and permitted_control. The first two call actual pipelineDecode; the last explicitly follows the interface ordering and is an unmonitored observation control. Every request is paired with its exact returned and consumed future. order_admitted is emitted after production but before decoder delivery. order_result is emitted after decoder completion. Auxiliary raw response fields are read from the original response storage, not treated as valid successful results when Error is nonnil.
semantic_changes: A forwarding future wrapper records only Error return and first Response invocation; it delegates original values and does not pre-call Error.
A pipeline proxy delivers that same wrapped real future to an isolated real decoder; transport producer output is otherwise unchanged.
The decoder receiver and followerReplication are minimally initialized; no leadership prefix is claimed. Empty requests exclude match-index and application effects.
Timeout is generated by actual InmemTransport; tool timeouts call t.Fatal and do not emit a completed comparison.
The permitted control uses a separate operation and future; it never supplies history for either decoder case.

legality.derivation: Use actual in-memory transport request enqueue, completion decoder, and per-request future identity. A connected receiver without a worker yields the transport own timeout. Successful cases create an unbootstrapped empty follower through NewRaft using empty real in-memory stores, then send a protocol-version-matched empty term-1 AppendEntries request with no predecessor or commit index. The real worker produces its reply. This is a local RPC/consumer contract input, not an elected-leader history. pipelineDecode is invoked with minimal peer and notification state; empty entries cannot reach commitment.match. No target logic is replaced.
legality.applicability: Method ordering before response interpretation requires no quorum, elected leadership, log entry, or FSM action. The isolated consumer has no concurrent writers. Receiver workers stay live through successful reply; timeout case omits receiver processing as its declared delay fault. Consumer stop is supplied after response entry or natural decoder termination, and completion is awaited before result observation.
unresolved: The harness does not establish the synthetic sender as a legally elected leader; this is excluded from the local claim.
The network transport and configuration transitions remain outside this execution.
alternatives: A full cluster history would be needed for a claim about decision safety but does not determine this interface method order.

grounding.derivation: Observe the actual pipelineDecode call through a forwarding AppendFuture wrapper. Error records return only after delegating to the real completed future. First Response entry records whether Error already returned. The property is response_accessed implies error_returned_before_response, never an equality between response success and RPC success.
grounding.applicability: Two isolated decoder operations receive independently produced real in-memory futures: a timeout with an unserviced receiver, and a successful empty append processed by a real NewRaft follower. Consumer completion and stable operation identity are recorded separately from the result.
unresolved: Network pipeline branch is not executed.
No leader election prefix, log commitment or application consequence is exercised.
alternatives: The real transport publishes after completion, protecting write visibility; this does not perform the required Error invocation.
Timeout response remains zero-valued and does not advance match support.

observable_properties.description: For each completed decoder operation, if Response was accessed on its admitted future then Error must already have returned on that same future.

uncertainties: Only the in-memory producer is executed; network producer support is sourced but not execution coverage.
A contract mismatch does not establish use of invalid successful support: the timeout response remains false and the successful reply comes from the actual follower.
The unbootstrapped follower and supplied term-1 request are an RPC prefix for this local interface check, not a proven election history.
